rationale: Commerce One gives a full third-party IP infringement defence and indemnity extending to us and our Customers, with the usual exclusions (use outside Documentation, third-party modification) and remedies (procure, replace/modify, terminate and refund), and Section 9 places Section 8 liability outside the cap. This meets the fallback position; there is no Customer-side indemnity to narrow. We may still ask for breach-of-law, data-breach and gross negligence/wilful misconduct limbs if the deal reopens.

If ongoing support is the concern, we can instead grant Commerce One a licence to the supported Developments.

rationale: Section 13.5 starts correctly (Developments created solely by Corio are owned by Corio, with an assignment from Commerce One) but the proviso strips our ownership of our own interface code whenever Commerce One supports it on an ongoing basis — an assignment of Customer IP to the Vendor, which is our walk-away. ruleTitle: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have reset the cap to the greater of 12 months' fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000 (the current per-transaction "amount actually paid" basis is illusory) and added the standard Excluded Claims so that confidentiality/data security, indemnities, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement sit outside the cap, with our fee obligations excluded from the cap. Fallback: a mutual 12-month fees cap with carve-outs at least for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct.

ops.newText: EXCEPT FOR EXCLUDED CLAIMS, IN NO EVENT SHALL EITHER PARTY'S LIABILITY ARISING OUT OF THIS AGREEMENT OR THE USE OR PERFORMANCE OF THE SOFTWARE EXCEED THE GREATER OF (A) THE TOTAL AMOUNT PAID OR PAYABLE BY CORIO HEREUNDER DURING THE TWELVE (12) MONTHS IMMEDIATELY PRIOR TO THE EVENT GIVING RISE TO THE CLAIM AND (B) USD 1,000,000. "EXCLUDED CLAIMS" MEANS A PARTY'S BREACH OF ITS CONFIDENTIALITY, DATA PROTECTION OR SECURITY OBLIGATIONS, ITS INDEMNIFICATION OBLIGATIONS UNDER SECTION 8, ITS GROSS NEGLIGENCE, WILFUL MISCONDUCT OR FRAUD, AND ITS INFRINGEMENT OF THE OTHER PARTY'S INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY RIGHTS; CORIO'S OBLIGATION TO PAY FEES SHALL NOT BE TREATED AS DAMAGES SUBJECT TO THIS CAP.
ops.oldText: EXCEPT FOR LIABILITY ARISING UNDER SECTION 8 OF THIS AGREEMENT, IN NO EVENT SHALL EITHER PARTY'S LIABILITY ARISING OUT OF THIS AGREEMENT OR THE USE OR PERFORMANCE OF THE SOFTWARE EXCEED THE TOTAL AMOUNT ACTUALLY PAID BY CORIO HEREUNDER FOR THE TRANSACTION WHICH THE LIABILITY RELATES TO DURING THE TWELVE (12) MONTHS IMMEDIATELY PRIOR TO THE FILING OF THE CAUSE OF ACTION TO WHICH THE LIABILITY RELATES.

proposal.summary: Make the cap a greater-of 12 months' fees / USD 1M and add standard uncapped carve-outs

quote: IN NO EVENT SHALL EITHER PARTY'S LIABILITY ARISING OUT OF THIS AGREEMENT OR THE USE OR PERFORMANCE OF THE SOFTWARE EXCEED THE TOTAL AMOUNT ACTUALLY PAID BY CORIO HEREUNDER FOR THE TRANSACTION WHICH THE LIABILITY RELATES TO DURING THE TWELVE (12) MONTHS IMMEDIATELY PRIOR TO THE FILING OF THE CAUSE OF ACTION
rationale: The cap is nominally mutual but the basis is narrow and illusory: only amounts "actually paid" by Corio and only "for the transaction which the liability relates to", with no greater-of USD 1,000,000 floor. Carve-outs are limited to Section 8 (IP indemnity); confidentiality/data security, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement sit inside the cap, and our fee obligations are not excluded. Redline resets the basis to 12 months' fees paid or payable / USD 1M and adds Excluded Claims.
ruleTitle: Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We must be able to assign to affiliates without consent and any consent for other assignments should not be unreasonably withheld; the existing M&A carve-out is retained. Fallback: mutual right to assign to affiliates and successors on written notice.

ops.newText: Neither party may assign this Agreement or any rights or obligations hereunder, whether by operation of law or otherwise, without the prior written consent of the other party, which shall not be unreasonably withheld or delayed; provided that Corio may assign this Agreement, in whole or in part, to any of its affiliates without such consent.
ops.oldText: Neither party may assign this Agreement or any rights or obligations hereunder, whether by operation of law or otherwise, without the prior written consent of the other party.

proposal.summary: Add affiliate assignment right for Customer and a reasonableness standard on consent

quote: Neither party may assign this Agreement or any rights or obligations hereunder, whether by operation of law or otherwise, without the prior written consent of the other party.
rationale: The M&A carve-out is present and there is no Vendor termination or re-pricing right on our change of control, but consent is at absolute discretion (no reasonableness standard) and there is no carve-out for assignment to our affiliates, and the competitor exception cuts back our M&A freedom. Redline adds an affiliate carve-out for Corio and a reasonableness standard, keeping the rest intact.

quote: Under no circumstances shall Commerce One contact Corio Customers regarding a non-ASP license sale, unless requested to do so by Corio.
rationale: All licences are non-exclusive and there is no obligation on us to source hosted procurement software only from Commerce One, to route customers exclusively through it, or to refrain from procuring from third parties; Exhibit D cooperation is expressly non-binding. The only channel restraint (Section 2.4) runs in our favour, which is acceptable.

quote: Maintenance and Support Fees: Net 30 of Software acceptance anniversary date, and each year thereafter. Revenue Sharing Fees: Quarterly payments shall be due to receiving party, net 30 days after quarter close.
rationale: There are no liquidated damages, penalties, late-payment interest, shortfall charges or minimum termination payments payable by us; the only money consequences of failure run in our favour (refund of prepaid fees on warranty breach under Section 7.3 and pro-rata refund under Section 8.1). No redline required.
ruleTitle: Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Our licences must cover our affiliates and the contractors we use to deliver the Corio Services (consistent with Section 14.8), so we have added them to the grant; the perpetual/irrevocable nature and successor transfer under Section 14.1 are unchanged. Fallback: affiliates covered on written notice to Commerce One.

ops.newText: Commerce One hereby grants to Corio and its affiliates and contractors acting on its behalf a fee-bearing, perpetual and irrevocable, nonexclusive, nontransferable
ops.oldText: Commerce One hereby grants to Corio a fee-bearing, perpetual and irrevocable, nonexclusive, nontransferable

proposal.summary: Extend the hosting licence to Customer affiliates and contractors acting on its behalf

quote: Commerce One hereby grants to Corio a fee-bearing, perpetual and irrevocable, nonexclusive, nontransferable (except in accordance with Section 14.1 of this Agreement), right and license in the Territory
rationale: The grant is perpetual and irrevocable and transferable on an M&A per Section 14.1, which is good, but it runs to Corio alone: our affiliates and the contractors we are expressly permitted to use under Section 14.8 are not covered, with no path to add them. Redline inserts affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf into the hosting grant.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept restrictions on the markets we may serve, so we have deleted the "Corio Market Segment" field-of-use limit from the definition of Customers (the North America Territory limit remains, with the expansion path in Section 2.10). Fallback: retain the revenue threshold but keep the existing growth/M&A carve-out and add a right to serve larger customers on notice to Commerce One.

ops.oldText: who obtains a sublicense from Corio to use the Software or MarketSite.net Service, in the Corio Market Segment.

quote: "CUSTOMER(S)" means one or more customers of the Corio Services having its principal executive offices in the Territory who obtains a sublicense from Corio to use the Software or MarketSite.net Service, in the Corio Market Segment.
rationale: There is no express covenant not to compete, but the "Corio Market Segment" definition (customers with annual sales revenue under USD 1,000,000,000) operates as a field-of-use restriction on the customers we may serve with the hosted Software, reinforced by the North America Territory limit. Our position is no field-of-use restriction on Customer; we have deleted the segment limit, with the fallback of retaining the threshold plus the existing growth/M&A carve-out and a notice-based right to serve larger customers.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] The five-year initial term gives us no exit absent breach, so we have added a Corio right to terminate for convenience on 30 days' notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees. Fallback: 60–90 days' notice with an early-termination fee capped at three months' fees.

ops.text: 11.1A Termination for Convenience. Corio may terminate this Agreement for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Commerce One, in which case Commerce One shall refund to Corio any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination. Commerce One shall have no right to terminate this Agreement for convenience during the initial term or any renewal term.

proposal.summary: Add Customer termination for convenience on 30 days' notice with refund of prepaid fees

quote: The term of this Agreement shall commence on the Effective Date and shall continue in full force and effect for an initial period of five (5) years.
rationale: In a five-year committed term we have no termination-for-convenience right at all: Section 11.2 allows termination only for uncured material breach or insolvency. Absence of a Customer convenience right in a multi-year term is a deviation; we have added a 30-day convenience right with refund of prepaid fees and confirmed Commerce One has no reciprocal walk-away.

quote: Such inspections may be made no more than once each calendar year, at reasonable times and upon reasonable notice. Commerce One shall bear all costs and expenses of such inspection. If any such inspection discloses a shortfall or an overpayment, the appropriate party shall promptly pay the amount of such shortfall or refund such overpayment. In addition, if any such inspection reveals an underpayment of more than five percent (5%) for the period under audit, Corio shall reimburse Commerce One for the reasonable cost of the examination.
rationale: Section 4.4 already matches our preferred position: once per calendar year, reasonable notice and business hours, by an independent CPA reasonably acceptable to us, records-only with no access to our systems, and Commerce One bears the cost unless underpayment exceeds 5%. No redline required.

quote: This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of the State of California, USA, excluding conflict of laws provisions and excluding the 1980 United Nations Convention on Contracts for the International Sale of Goods. Any disputes arising out of this Agreement shall be resolved by binding arbitration in accordance with the then-current commercial arbitration rules of the American Arbitration Association ("RULES").
rationale: California law is on our accepted list and the AAA arbitration is seated domestically in San Francisco County with awards enforceable in the California courts, so this is not the walk-away case of a foreign seat or an unaccepted home jurisdiction. Our preference remains courts rather than arbitration, but we would not spend negotiating capital here.

quote: Corio Customer Application Management Revenue: Corio to pay Commerce One [*] of all Application Management Revenue from Corio Customers for use of Commerce One Software or MarketSite.net Service Access subject to the following limitations.
rationale: Exhibit B sets fixed pricing and revenue-share percentages with no most-favoured-nation or best-terms mechanic in either direction, and nothing obliges us to extend Commerce One terms no less favourable than those we give third parties or to match third-party offers. No redline required.

quote: No Application Management Revenue shall be due for any Corio Customer subscriptions utilizing the initial 3000 Software User licenses granted herein, subject to a minimum limitation of 40 Authorized Software Users per Customer
rationale: There is no take-or-pay, volume commitment or shortfall payment on us: Software Users are unlimited, revenue-share fees accrue only on revenue we actually receive once a Customer goes live, and Implementation Fees are time-and-materials subject to a cap. The 40-user reference is a threshold for the revenue-share exemption, not a purchase commitment. No redline required.
ruleTitle: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer

quote: The parties are independent contractors with respect to each other.
rationale: A full-text search for solicitation, hiring, employment and inducement language returns nothing; Sections 5, 13 and Exhibit D deal with personnel access and dedicated sales resources without any hiring restriction, and there is no no-hire. This matches our preferred position (no non-solicit on Customer).

quote: Thereafter, this Agreement shall automatically renew for subsequent one (1) year periods unless either party provides the other party with written notification at least thirty (30) days prior to the expiration of the initial five (5) year term or any one (1) year renewal thereof of its intention to terminate this Agreement.
rationale: Renewals are 12 months (not multi-year) and the non-renewal notice window is 30 days, at our preferred level; Exhibit B pre-agrees the Year 2-5 "and beyond" maintenance and MarketSite fees, so there is no unilateral uplift right to cap. No redline required.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 11.3 addresses survival but not exit: we have added transition assistance for up to six months at then-current rates plus return of our and our Customers' data in machine-readable form within 30 days and certified deletion thereafter. Fallback: 90 days of transition assistance with data export within 30 days.

ops.text: 11.4 Transition Assistance and Return of Data. Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Commerce One shall (a) at Corio's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Commerce One's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days of Corio's request, return to Corio all Corio and Customer data in Commerce One's possession or control in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete such data from its systems and certify such deletion to Corio in writing.

proposal.summary: Insert post-termination transition assistance and data return/deletion obligation

quote: Upon termination or expiration of this Agreement, each party shall otherwise return or destroy any Confidential Information of the other party provided, however, Corio may retain any Confidential Information necessary for Corio to continue supporting it's then-existing Customers.
rationale: Section 11.3 covers survival and return of Confidential Information but there is no transition-assistance obligation and no obligation on Commerce One to return our or our Customers' data in a usable format or to certify deletion — the source-code escrow in Section 12 is not a substitute. We have inserted a transition and data-return clause (six months' assistance, 30-day machine-readable export, certified deletion).
ruleTitle: Post-termination transition assistance and data return

proposal.comment: [Playbook] A 60-day warranty running from the Effective Date (and expiring on a fixed calendar date) gives us almost no coverage for a five-year hosted deployment, so we have set the Warranty Period at twelve (12) months from delivery. Fallback: ninety (90) days from delivery with the same repair/replace/refund remedies.

ops.oldText: for a period of sixty (60) days from the Effective Date, but in no event not later than December 31, 1999 (the "Warranty Period")

quote: for a period of sixty (60) days from the Effective Date, but in no event not later than December 31, 1999 (the "Warranty Period")
rationale: There is an express conformance warranty with adequate remedies (correction, replacement, termination and refund) and a no-malicious-code warranty, but the Warranty Period is only 60 days and runs from the Effective Date with a hard December 31, 1999 cut-off — below our fallback of 90 days from delivery and effectively expiring before the five-year hosted deployment matures.
